Olive Tree

precepts.text: The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.
precepts.point: Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off: Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off. And thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear. Where did we read that? Zechariah 12:7: that they do not magnify themselves against Judah. That magnify is telling you: don't be highminded. Don't boast.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“And if some of the branches be broken off”. The branches broken off are Judah. Jeremiah shows the olive tree and its breaking: “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.”

God himself named his people a green olive tree, fair and of goodly fruit. That is the tree Paul speaks of. And the fire kindled on it with a great tumult is how the branches came to be broken.

Why were they broken? Paul answers: “because of unbelief they were broken off”. Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off.

So when the wild olive tree, the northern kingdom, is graffed in among them, it is graffed into God's own green olive tree. “Boast not against the branches”: do not boast against Judah. “thou bearest not the root, but the root thee”. The root is Christ, and Christ is the one that keeps the northern kingdom graffed in with Judah. “Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.”

precepts.text: The Lord called thy name a green olive tree; he hath kindled fire upon it and the branches of it are broken, for the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah.
precepts.point: As concerning the gospel they are enemies for your sakes, but as touching the election they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. As ye in times past had not believed God but now have obtained mercy through their unbelief, so they through your mercy may obtain mercy. God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all: all Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Who is the olive tree? Jeremiah shows it: “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.” The branches of it are broken, just as Paul referenced.

Then watch who that olive tree is: “For the Lord of hosts, that planted thee, hath pronounced evil against thee, for the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which they have done against themselves to provoke me to anger in offering incense unto Baal.” The house of Israel first, the house of Judah second: both houses.

So the olive tree refers to both the house of Israel and the house of Judah. The wild olive tree is not the other nations; the nations are never called olive trees.

That is how Romans 11 ends: “God is able to graff them in again.” Again, because they were always there. “And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.” Their sins, Jacob’s sins, all twelve tribes. The white man did many sins on this earth, and the Lord is not taking his sins away; he is going to pay for them. “God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all”: all Israel.

precepts.text: I will bring evil upon them which they shall not be able to escape; the curses shall overtake thee, meaning you will not escape them.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“Therefore thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will bring evil upon them, which they shall not be able to escape; and though they shall cry unto me, I will not hearken unto them.” That is what overtake thee means: the curses shall overtake thee, meaning you shall not be able to escape them.

And notice the turn. Israel would not hearken unto his voice, so when the evil comes and they cry unto him, he will not hearken unto them. The curses come upon thee and overtake thee, and there is no escaping them.

precepts.text: The Lord called thy name a green olive tree, fair and of goodly fruit; we are that green olive tree.
precepts.point: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God; I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.” Jeremiah tells who the green olive tree is: “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit”. We are that green olive tree. The Lord called Israel by that name, fair and of goodly fruit, and though “with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken”, David stands as the green olive tree in the house of God, trusting in his mercy for ever.

precepts.text: Cursed is everyone that confirms not all the words of this law to do them.
precepts.point: Hear the words of this covenant: cursed be the man that obeys not its words.
precepts.why:
The curse Jeremiah is told to speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem is the curse of the law itself. Moses had already said it: “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them. And all the people shall say, Amen.” Our fathers answered Amen to it.

So when the Lord says “Cursed be the man that obeyeth not the words of this covenant”, he is holding Israel to the very words they agreed to. The covenant is the law, and the curse is on everyone that confirms not all of its words to do them.

precepts.text: As many as are of the works of the law are under the curse without continuing in all things written.
precepts.point: Hear the words of this covenant: cursed be the man that obeys not its words.
precepts.why:
Paul repeats the same curse: “Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.” The curse Jeremiah was sent to proclaim did not pass away with the prophets; it is written in the New Testament word for word.

“For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse”. It is not enough to start in the law; the man that does not continue in all things written in the book is under the curse. That is the man Jeremiah 11:3 is speaking of, the man that obeys not the words of this covenant.

precepts.text: All these curses come on those who will not obey the voice of the Lord.
precepts.point: Hear the words of this covenant: cursed be the man that obeys not its words.
precepts.why:
Here is what the curse on the man that obeys not looks like: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

The words of the covenant are his commandments and his statutes. To not obey the voice of the Lord is to not observe to do them, and all these curses come on that man and overtake him. That is the curse Jeremiah is sent to remind Judah and Jerusalem of.

precepts.text: Israel is the green olive tree whose branches are broken for the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
precepts.point: Ephraim is the wild olive tree grafted back in among the tribes, partaking of the root and fatness, and Paul warns them not to boast against the branches. The north believed on Christ while much of the south, the Pharisees, stumbled at him, but that is no ground to boast.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.”

Israel is the green olive tree. Its branches were broken “for the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which they have done against themselves to provoke me to anger in offering incense unto Baal.” Both houses are branches of the one tree, and both were broken for their evil. That is why the one grafted back in is no stranger to the tree, and why neither may boast against the other.

points: Hear the words of this covenant: cursed be the man that obeys not its words.
He commanded the fathers from the iron furnace of Egypt to obey His voice, so they would be His people and He their God, to perform the oath to give a land flowing with milk and honey.

Just as you see the brothers in purple and gold out on the corners teaching every day in IUIC, the prophets did the exact same thing, proclaiming the words of the covenant in the streets. The thing that has been is that which shall be.

He earnestly protested to the fathers from the day He brought them out of Egypt, rising early and saying obey My voice, yet they obeyed not but walked in the imagination of their evil heart; therefore He brings on them all the words of this covenant.

A conspiracy is found among the men of Judah; they turned back to the iniquities of their fathers and went after other gods. Therefore He will bring evil they cannot escape, and though they cry to Him He will not hearken. This is the people crying and praying only after Little Ray Ray gets shot, when Ray Ray was a drug dealer, a fornicator, and a murderer, and the no-snitching mentality shielded a killer. Now they cry and the Lord says He will not hear them.

The cities of Judah cry to the gods to whom they burn incense, but those gods cannot save them in the time of trouble. When all hell breaks loose on our people, they go pray to white-man Jesus. According to the number of their cities were their gods.
Therefore pray not for this people, neither lift up a cry or prayer for them, for He will not hear them in the time they cry to Him for their trouble.

What has His beloved to do in His house, having wrought lewdness with many. He had called her name a green olive tree fair and of goodly fruit, but with a great tumult He kindles fire on it and breaks its branches, for the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, the northern and southern kingdoms, done to provoke Him.

The Lord gave the prophet knowledge of their doings, but he had been like a lamb or ox brought to the slaughter, not knowing they had devised devices against him to destroy the tree with its fruit and cut him off from the land of the living. He commits his cause to the Lord who judges righteously and asks to see His vengeance on them.

Against the men of Anathoth who sought his life and told him not to prophesy in the name of the Lord, He will punish them: the young men die by the sword, their sons and daughters by famine, and no remnant will be left in the year of their visitation.
